newsitem.title: USA: Washington Republican leaders welcome budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Washington Republican leaders welcome budget plan.

text.p: Republican legislative leaders on Tuesday welcomed Washington Gov. Gary Locke's two-year spending plan, which cuts social services to increase school funding and jail time for juvenile criminals.
"The governor's budget sets priorities we agree with," said Republican Senate majority leader Dan McDonald.
"It was a very encouraging start," echoed Republican Speaker of the House Clyde Ballard.
Washington state spending will increase at the slowest rate in 25 years under the budget plan unveiled Tuesday morning by the state's Democratic governor.

Locke's $19.2 billion state budget for the next two years comes in under the spending cap set in a recent voter initiative. Locke cut social services to fund increased spending on education and increased sentences for the most serious juvenile offenders.
State lawmakers will work through the budget's details in the coming weeks. Senate Republicans plan to begin hearings and debate on their proposed revisions around March 24.
The state's biggest teachers union urged legislators to stick with the governor's proposed pay raises for educators and other state workers.
They would get a 2.5 percent cost-of-living pay hike this year and against next year.
"Governor Locke is keeping his promise to Washington's public schools," said C.T. Purdom, president of the Washington Education Association. "Now it's time for lawmakers to keep theirs."
Lobbyists for the poor said they are worried conservative lawmakers may expand on the already "painful" social service cuts in the governor's budget.
"We would hope the legislature would not go below (Locke's) budget in terms of funding human services," said Tony Lee, a lobbyist for a Seattle non-profit aid agency.
